groups.text: It is currently a clear morning in Berlin-Tempelhof with a temperature of 21 degrees.
With the morning weather set, here is the news.

South African fintech startup TurnStay has processed over 61.5 million dollars in travel payments during the first six months of this year. Founded three years ago by Alon Stern and James Hedley, the company uses a merchant-of-record model and stablecoins to settle funds locally for African travel businesses. This system reduces payment fees by up to 70 percent compared to traditional processing, which can cost merchants as much as eight percent per transaction. TurnStay is now preparing for a Series A raise following previous seed funding rounds. In other news, Paris Saint-Germain and Aston Villa face off this Wednesday in the UEFA Super Cup final at the Red Bull Arena in Salzburg, Austria. The match pits the Champions League winner, PSG, against Europa League champion Aston Villa. Fans can watch the game starting at 4 p.m. Brasília time via SBT, TNT Sports, or HBO Max.

Vladimir Putin has threatened that Moscow will respond in kind if European countries seize Russian commercial vessels. Speaking during exercises of Russia's Pacific Fleet, Putin called such attempts piracy and claimed they violate international maritime law. This tension rises as Western nations ramp up efforts to clamp down on Russia's shadow fleet. These aging and poorly insured tankers are used by Moscow to carry out hybrid operations and circumvent sanctions. Recently, the United Kingdom, France, Belgium, and Sweden have intercepted vessels from this fleet, many of which sailed under third-country flags. In one concrete result of these seizures, Swedish courts agreed to hand over a shadow fleet vessel named Caffa to Ukraine. The ship was transporting grain looted from occupied Ukrainian territories. The U.S. has also seized a Russian-flagged tanker as part of the broader effort to restrict Moscow's economic operators.

In England and Wales, the chief inspector of probation warns that an early release scheme for 5,000 offenders starting in October could lead to serious sexual offenses, violent crimes, or murder. Martin Jones says probation services are already under unprecedented pressure managing 258,000 cases, leaving him lacking confidence that the system can cope with the increase. While the government aims to ease prison overcrowding, fifty UK police chiefs have urged the prime minister to prevent the release of those who killed PC Andrew Harper. Elsewhere, software company Ivanti has issued patches for four vulnerabilities in its Endpoint Manager and Neurons for MDM products. These flaws could allow remote attackers to leak SQL credentials or crash agent services, though Ivanti reports no known exploits. Meanwhile, in Indonesia, a ferry called the Putri Yasmin caught fire between Bali and Lombok. One 19-year-old woman died, while 172 others were rescued from the flames.

Anthropic is implementing watermarks on text and images generated by its Claude AI to make synthetic content easier to identify. This move follows the requirements of the European AI Act, which mandates technical detection markings for AI-generated or manipulated media. Under Article 50 of the law, these obligations apply to generative AI models marketed in the EU since August 2nd, while existing models have a grace period until December 2nd. Anthropic is deploying a dual marking system for its newest models, including an invisible statistical marker for text. These transparency measures are required by law, though some exceptions exist if the content has undergone human review or editorial control. By adopting these tools, Anthropic also aligns with a voluntary code of practice on AI content transparency.

Russia-linked shipping is scrambling to reduce its exposure to Ukraine’s expanding maritime campaign across the Black Sea and Sea of Azov. The sanctioned suezmax tanker Caruzo provides a visible example of these improvised defenses. Photographs show the vessel passing Istanbul with netting over the accommodation block and cage-like structures suspended over the aft section. These additions aim to protect the superstructure from aerial drones and provide stand-off protection for the engine room against uncrewed surface vessels. Beyond physical armor, Russia is changing how its ships sail. The Russian-flagged tanker Strateg previously drew attention by hugging the Turkish coastline rather than crossing open waters. This shift in route planning suggests a desire for the relative protection offered by proximity to Turkey. These low-tech barriers and coastal routes mark a significant adaptation as Ukraine continues to target commercial shipping associated with the Russian economy.

Tuesday was primary election day across six US states, leaving several key races undecided or shifting toward new leadership. In Minnesota, the progressive Lieutenant Governor won the Democratic Senate primary by defeating Representative Angie Craig. The state's Republican governor’s primary saw House Speaker Lisa Demuth defeat Mike Lindell, a businessman endorsed by Donald Trump. Meanwhile, Wisconsin’s Republican gubernatorial primary remains too close to call. In South Carolina, Darlene Graham has advanced to the Republican Senate runoff. She is seeking to succeed her brother, Lindsay Graham, who died suddenly last month. Both major parties are now preparing for runoffs in several of these contested races.

A group of physicians and experts are warning clinicians about potential safety issues tied to Vykat XR, a drug sold by Neurocrine Biosciences for Prader-Willi syndrome. While not definitively linked, the FDA’s Adverse Event Monitoring System has recorded seven deaths and over 100 reports of serious adverse events, including heart and respiratory complications, since the drug's March 2025 approval. In legal news, Meta returns to court this Wednesday in California. A coalition of U.S. attorneys general aims to prove that Facebook and Instagram were deliberately designed to be addictive for minors. Meanwhile, Check Point reports that North Korean hackers from the Lazarus Group have exploited a Windows zero-day vulnerability to seize control of systems. Targeting aerospace and aviation organizations in India and Europe through fake job offers, the attackers deployed the ForestTiger backdoor before Microsoft patched the flaw on August 11.
After the headlines, back to the weather.
This afternoon will remain clear with temperatures between 21 and 26 degrees.
And from the weather, a quick look at the calendar.
On your calendar today: personal calendar: all day: Sommerferien 2026 Berlin, at 10:00, Optikrunde, at 15:00, Gruppenmeeting Gregor, and at 19:00, Bitcoin Socratic Seminar.
Mail worth checking: Maschinenstuermer sent an update regarding the release of version 1.2.0 in hackumenta.
And that's it for your personal morning broadcast.
[mature adult voice, intensely emotional, tender, radiant; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
[very very long pause before speaking; then mature adult voice, most emotional, strong, warm, radiant, deeply encouraging; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
